blocks.prompt: 1 (i) Find all the antiderivatives for each derivative: \(\frac{dy}{dx} = 100x^4\)
blocks.explanation:
We are given the derivative of \(y\) and must find \(y\) itself: this is antidifferentiation.
"All the antiderivatives" means the whole family, so the answer must carry \(+\,c\).
Plan: take the constant 100 outside (Rule 1) and use the Power Rule (Rule 3).
steps:
Given: \(\frac{dy}{dx} = 100x^4\).
To find: every function \(y\) with this derivative.
Method: \(y = \int 100x^4\,dx\). Rule 1 takes the constant out, Rule 3 integrates \(x^4\): add 1 to the power and divide by the new power.

Write \(y\) as an integral
\[y = \int 100x^4\,dx\]
\[= 100\int x^4\,dx\]
Why: Rule 1, \(\int k f(x)\,dx = k\int f(x)\,dx\). A constant factor can come outside the integral sign.

Apply the Power Rule
\[= 100\cdot\dfrac{x^{4+1}}{4+1} + c\]
\[= 100\cdot\dfrac{x^5}{5} + c\]
\[= 20x^5 + c\]
Why: Rule 3, \(\int x^n\,dx = \frac{x^{n+1}}{n+1} + c\) with \(n = 4 \ne -1\).

Check
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(20x^5 + c\right) = 100x^4 \;\checkmark\]
Why: Differentiating the answer must give back the given derivative; the derivative of the constant \(c\) is 0.
blocks.final_answer: \(y = 20x^5 + c\), where \(c\) is an arbitrary constant (each value of \(c\) gives one antiderivative).

blocks.prompt: 1 (ii) Find all the antiderivatives for each derivative: \(\frac{dy}{dt} = 2 + 24t^3 - 10t^4\)
blocks.explanation:
Again the derivative is given and \(y\) is wanted, but now the variable is \(t\).
The right side is a sum of three terms, so we integrate term by term.
Plan: Rule 2 (sum/difference), Rule 1 (constants out), Rule 3 (Power Rule), one constant \(c\) at the end.
steps:
Given: \(\frac{dy}{dt} = 2 + 24t^3 - 10t^4\).
To find: all functions \(y\) of \(t\) with this derivative.
Method: \(y = \int (2 + 24t^3 - 10t^4)\,dt\). Split the integral term by term (Rule 2), take out constants (Rule 1), then use the Power Rule on each power of \(t\).

Split the integral term by term
\[y = \int 2\,dt + \int 24t^3\,dt - \int 10t^4\,dt\]
\[= 2\int 1\,dt + 24\int t^3\,dt - 10\int t^4\,dt\]
Why: Rule 2 lets us integrate a sum or difference one term at a time; Rule 1 takes each constant outside.

Integrate each term
\[= 2t + 24\cdot\dfrac{t^4}{4} - 10\cdot\dfrac{t^5}{5} + c\]
\[= 2t + 6t^4 - 2t^5 + c\]
Why: \(\int 1\,dt = t\), and the Power Rule gives \(\frac{t^4}{4}\) and \(\frac{t^5}{5}\). The three separate constants add up to one arbitrary constant \(c\).

Check
\[\dfrac{d}{dt}\left(2t + 6t^4 - 2t^5 + c\right)\]
\[= 2 + 24t^3 - 10t^4 \;\checkmark\]
Why: Differentiating gives back exactly the given derivative.
